To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mean climate state simulated by cloud‐resolving RCE is characterized by a large number of TCs that are relatively small in size, but intense, with a cold‐point troposphere that is higher than the nonrotating RCT.
the average number of tropical cyclones in TC World decreases with increasing SST while the TCs' intensity, size, and per‐cyclone precipitation rate increase with increasing SST.
TCs are an integral part of rotating RCE and the mean state of the Tropics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mean climate state of the tropical atmosphere in which multiple TCs coexist.
the mean state and the variability of the TC World and its response to SST changes.
the role of TCs in the tropical climate system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TCs in TC World tend to become more intense, but less numerous, with increasing SST, and that the TC World's mean precipitation rate increases with SST, but less rapidly than that in nonrotating simulations.
TC World is a more realistic RCE than nonrotating Rce, and it is a good candidate for the idealization of the mean tropical climate.
TC World is a more realistic representation of the mean Tropics than nonrotating Rce.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TCs are a major component of RCE in the Tropies and that their presence affects RCE in several ways, including the outflow temperature, the cold‐point troposphere height, the vertical distribution of water vapor, and the vertical structure of the tropical circulation.
the TC World, as a mean tropical climate with TCs, exhibits a much more robust response to SST change than the nonrotating Rce.
the tropical mean state is characterized by a trade‐off between the TC activity and the cold‐point troposphere height.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of rotation, the tropical cyclones are the dominant convective elements, and the tropical circulation is organized by them.
the mean tropical circulation is a complex interplay between TCs and the large‐scale circulation, and that TCs are an essential part of the mean tropical circulation.

the tropical cyclone activity in TC World is much more vigorous than in the nonrotating Rce and that the mean state in the Tropies is likely to be significantly affected by tropical cyclones, especially in the case of a warming climate.
